_about: Routes for Pokémon that can't be obtained by normal play or trading: self-hosted events (kind 'event') and glitches (kind 'glitch'). Keyed by game, then national dex number; each entry lists routes in order of preference. Methods are for English cartridges unless noted.

eventTicket.name: Self-hosted event: inject the event ticket
eventTicket.steps: Back up your save. Download the official Wonder Card (.wc3) for your exact game from Project Pokémon, open your save in suloku's Gen 3 Mystery Gift Tool and inject it, then save. In-game, collect the ticket from the delivery man in green inside any Poké Mart, then take the ferry to the island and catch the Pokémon yourself. Emerald boats leave from Lilycove; FireRed/LeafGreen Seagallop ferries from Vermilion.
eventTicket.warning: Wonder Cards aren't interchangeable between Emerald and FireRed/LeafGreen: use the file made for your game. PKHeX can't inject Gen 3 Wonder Cards; use the Mystery Gift Tool. Works on emulator saves directly; real cartridges need a cart reader to copy the save off and back.

eventTrade.name: Self-hosted event: trade from a second save
eventTrade.steps: Make a second save that can trade with this game (a copy of your save works). Open it in PKHeX, add the event Pokémon from its Mystery Gift Database (the official distributions are listed there) and check the legality indicator, then save. Trade it over: two linked emulator instances, or two systems with a link cable.
eventTrade.warning: Back up both saves first. Use the same language as your game: Japanese Gen I/II Pokémon can crash non-Japanese games. Use a current PKHeX release, as some older ones had Gen I save bugs.

mewGlitch.name: Mew glitch (trainer escape / Trainer-Fly)
mewGlitch.steps: Stand where a long-range trainer (e.g. the Gambler near Lavender Town, or a Route 24 trainer) will spot you, and open the Start menu and use Fly (or Teleport) on the same step they see you. Fly to Cerulean City and battle the Youngster on Route 25 near Bill's house, making sure he walks up to you. Fly back to Lavender Town and walk west onto Route 8: the Start menu pops up by itself; close it and a level 7 Mew appears.
mewGlitch.warning: Harmless to your save, but follow the steps exactly. Save before starting.

celebiEgg.name: Celebi Egg glitch
celebiEgg.steps: Make a 'bad clone' with the PC box trick (deposit more Pokémon than you've ever deposited in a box), get a Day Care Egg from a Sneasel whose third move is Beat Up, then shuffle the Egg with 'PkMn w/o mail' moves and PC deposits so its move bytes overwrite its species. Hatch it to get Celebi.
celebiEgg.warning: Long and fiddly. It relies on save-corrupting tricks: back up your save first (use an emulator save state or a cartridge backup).

aceSetup.name: Arbitrary code execution (ACE) setup
aceSetup.steps: Get a glitch Egg of species 0x611 (Emerald/RS) or 0x351 (FireRed/LeafGreen) and use it to run code typed into your PC box names. Follow E-Sh4rk's ACE3 tutorial, then use the box-name codes from Sleipnir's lists.
aceSetup.warning: Works on real GBA hardware or the mGBA emulator (other emulators may not be accurate enough). Not for the Switch versions. Keep box 12–14 and the last row of box 11 empty when running codes, keep spare copies of the glitch Egg, and check each code worked before saving.
